Documentation → Releases → 1.15.0

SATOM 1.15.0

Sentinel's Architecture and Incidents console now open inside the Admin Console, next to its settings, instead of taking you to another page.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Architecture and Incidents console as panes
  • What changes for you
  • Under the hood
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-08-23 · All releases

In short#

The three entries of the Sentinel group in the Admin Console now all stay in the Admin Console. Architecture and the Incidents console open as panes beside the settings, and the buttons inside them keep you there. Operators and administrators who use Sentinel will notice.

What's new#

Architecture and Incidents console as panes#

Settings → Sentinel → Architecture and Settings → Sentinel → Incidents console now open inside the Admin Console instead of replacing the whole page. They show exactly the same content as their stand-alone pages:

  • Architecture — the architecture document, built from the live scoring weights, the list of response actions and the settings.
  • Incidents console — the live console with its four health tiles, the seven-day figures and the incident table.

Before, two of the three entries in the group took the whole page away and the only way back was the browser's Back button.

What changes for you#

  • Controls inside the panes keep you in the console. Running a sweep or rebuilding the baseline brings you back to the pane you started from. The status filter on the incident table reloads the Settings page instead of jumping to the stand-alone console, and the Architecture button switches to the neighbouring pane.
  • Opening a single incident still leaves the console, because an incident has a page of its own.
  • No Sentinel menu entry shows the "leaving" arrow any more, because none of them leaves the Admin Console.
  • The incident table scrolls sideways inside the pane. Its nine columns do not fit the narrower Admin Console column, and previously the table was cut off at the edge.
  • The user guide describes the three panes.

Under the hood#

  • The pane and the stand-alone page are drawn from the same source, so they cannot show different numbers.
  • The Settings page now works out the health of the metrics store once and shares it between the three Sentinel sections, instead of asking three times.
